command: SELECT column FROM table WHERE condition;

examples: SELECT name FROM students WHERE age > 16;

command: INSERT INTO table (col1, col2) VALUES (val1, val2);

command: UPDATE table SET column = value WHERE condition;
description: Update rows matching a condition
examples: UPDATE students SET age = 17 WHERE name = 'Alex';

examples: CREATE TABLE students (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT);

command: ALTER TABLE table ADD column TYPE;
description: Add a new column to a table
examples: ALTER TABLE students ADD email TEXT;

command: SELECT * FROM table ORDER BY column;
description: Sort results by a column
examples: SELECT * FROM students ORDER BY name;

command: SELECT * FROM table ORDER BY column DESC;
description: Sort results in descending order
examples: SELECT * FROM students ORDER BY age DESC;

command: SELECT * FROM table1 JOIN table2 ON condition;

examples: SELECT * FROM students JOIN grades ON students.id = grades.student_id;

description: Select unique values from a column

command: SELECT column FROM table WHERE column LIKE '%text%';
description: Search for a pattern within a column
examples: SELECT name FROM students WHERE name LIKE '%an%';

command: SELECT column FROM table GROUP BY column;
description: Group rows sharing a value
examples: SELECT subject FROM grades GROUP BY subject;

command: SELECT column, COUNT(*) FROM table GROUP BY column;
description: Count rows within each group
examples: SELECT subject, COUNT(*) FROM grades GROUP BY subject;

description: Choose several columns from a table

command: SELECT column AS alias FROM table;
description: Give a column a different name in the results
examples: SELECT name AS student_name FROM students;

command: SELECT * FROM table WHERE a = 1 AND b = 2;
description: Match rows where two conditions are both true
examples: SELECT * FROM students WHERE year = 11 AND grade > 5;

command: SELECT * FROM table WHERE a = 1 OR b = 2;
description: Match rows where at least one condition is true
examples: SELECT * FROM students WHERE year = 10 OR year = 11;

command: SELECT * FROM table WHERE NOT condition;
description: Match rows where a condition is false
examples: SELECT * FROM students WHERE NOT year = 7;

command: SELECT * FROM table WHERE column BETWEEN a AND b;
description: Match values within a range
examples: SELECT * FROM students WHERE age BETWEEN 14 AND 16;

command: SELECT * FROM table WHERE column IN (a, b, c);
description: Match values from a list
examples: SELECT * FROM students WHERE year IN (9, 10, 11);

command: SELECT * FROM table WHERE column IS NULL;
description: Find rows where a value is missing
examples: SELECT * FROM students WHERE email IS NULL;

command: SELECT * FROM table WHERE column LIKE 'A%';
description: Match text that starts with certain letters
examples: SELECT * FROM students WHERE name LIKE 'A%';

command: SELECT * FROM table ORDER BY col1, col2;
description: Sort by one column and then another
examples: SELECT * FROM students ORDER BY year, name;

command: SELECT * FROM table LIMIT n OFFSET m;

command: SELECT column FROM table GROUP BY column HAVING COUNT(*) > n;
description: Filter groups after counting them
examples: SELECT year, COUNT(*) FROM students GROUP BY year HAVING COUNT(*) > 30;

command: SELECT * FROM table1 INNER JOIN table2 ON t1.id = t2.id;
description: Combine rows that have a match in both tables
examples: SELECT * FROM students INNER JOIN classes ON students.class_id = classes.id;

command: SELECT * FROM table1 LEFT JOIN table2 ON condition;
description: Keep every row from the first table, with matches from the second
examples: SELECT * FROM students LEFT JOIN results ON students.id = results.student_id;

command: SELECT * FROM table1 RIGHT JOIN table2 ON condition;
description: Keep every row from the second table, with matches from the first
examples: SELECT * FROM results RIGHT JOIN students ON results.student_id = students.id;

command: SELECT * FROM table WHERE column > (SELECT AVG(column) FROM table);
description: Use the result of one query inside another (subquery)
examples: SELECT * FROM results WHERE score > (SELECT AVG(score) FROM results);

command: SELECT * FROM table1 UNION SELECT * FROM table2;
description: Combine the results of two queries into one list
examples: SELECT name FROM teachers UNION SELECT name FROM students;

description: Add a row giving a value for every column

command: UPDATE table SET col1 = a, col2 = b WHERE condition;
description: Change several columns in matching rows
examples: UPDATE students SET year = 11, class = '11A' WHERE id = 5;

command: SELECT CASE WHEN condition THEN a ELSE b END FROM table;
description: Choose different values depending on a condition
examples: SELECT CASE WHEN score >= 50 THEN 'Pass' ELSE 'Fail' END FROM results;

command: SELECT * FROM table ORDER BY RANDOM() LIMIT 1;

examples: SELECT * FROM questions ORDER BY RANDOM() LIMIT 1;

command: SELECT * FROM table1 FULL OUTER JOIN table2 ON condition;
description: Keep every row from both tables, matched where possible
examples: SELECT * FROM students FULL OUTER JOIN results ON students.id = results.student_id;

command: SELECT * FROM table1 CROSS JOIN table2;
description: Pair every row of one table with every row of another
examples: SELECT * FROM colours CROSS JOIN sizes;

command: SELECT * FROM table AS a JOIN table AS b ON a.x = b.y;
description: Join a table to itself
examples: SELECT e.name, m.name FROM staff e JOIN staff m ON e.manager_id = m.id;

command: SELECT * FROM t1 UNION ALL SELECT * FROM t2;
description: Combine two queries and keep duplicate rows
examples: SELECT name FROM a UNION ALL SELECT name FROM b;

command: SELECT * FROM t1 INTERSECT SELECT * FROM t2;
description: Return only the rows that appear in both queries
examples: SELECT name FROM a INTERSECT SELECT name FROM b;

command: SELECT * FROM t1 EXCEPT SELECT * FROM t2;
description: Return rows from the first query that are not in the second
examples: SELECT name FROM a EXCEPT SELECT name FROM b;

command: WITH name AS (SELECT ...) SELECT * FROM name;
description: Name a query so you can reuse it (common table expression)
examples: WITH adults AS (SELECT * FROM people WHERE age >= 18) SELECT * FROM adults;

command: SELECT ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY col) FROM table;
description: Number the rows in a chosen order
examples: SELECT name, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY score DESC) FROM results;

command: SELECT * FROM table WHERE column > ANY (SELECT ...);

command: SELECT * FROM table WHERE column REGEXP 'pattern';
